### Alternative proof of Proposition 6.1.1 
In __Proposition 6.1.1__, the author explicitly construct an exception set for teaching propose, however we can do it in another way:

For any constant $c$, we have 
$$
P(M_n\leq c)=P(\max_{1\leq i\leq n}X_n\leq c)=\prod_{i=1}^nP(X_i\leq c)=F^n(c)\to0.
$$

What we want to prove is
$$
P(M_n\to\infty)=1
$$
Since $M_n$ is increasing with $n$, so $M_n\to\sup_n M_n$, therefore it is suffice to prove
$$
P(\sup_n M_n=\infty)=1
$$
or
$$
P(\sup_n M_n<\infty)=0
$$

Note that
$$
\{\sup_n M_n<\infty\}=\bigcup_{m\in\mathbb Z}\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty\{M_n\leq m\}
$$
and for any $m$,
$$
P(\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty\{M_n\leq m\})=\lim_{n\to\infty}P(M_n\leq m)=0
$$
so
$$
P(\bigcup_{m\in\mathbb Z}\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty\{M_n\leq m\})\leq\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}P(\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty\{M_n\leq m\})=0.
$$
Therefore $P(\sup_n M_n<\infty)=0$, that is
$$
M_n\to\infty\quad \text{a.s.}
$$
